From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish cigarro.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [siˈɣa.ru]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic, Valencia) [siˈɣa.ro]

Noun

[edit]

cigarro m (plural cigarros)

  1. alternative form of cigar
  2. (colloquial) cigarette (thin roll of tobacco made for smoking)
    Synonyms: cigarret, cigarreta

Further reading

[edit]
  • “cigarro”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “cigarro” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

    Spanish

    [edit]
    Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
    cigarro
    Wikipedia es

    Etymology

    [edit]
    Etymology tree
    Latin cicādader.
    Vulgar Latin *cicār(r)a
    Spanish cigarra?
    Spanish cigarro

      Uncertain. Possiblities include:

      • Perhaps from cigarro (“male cicada”), a form of cigarra (“cicada”) found in some older texts particularly from southern Spain.[1]
      • From a Mayan language. Compare Yucatec Maya siyar (“to smoke tobacco leaves”), Q'eqchi sikʼar (“to smoke”).[2]

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /θiˈɡaro/ [θiˈɣ̞a.ro] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
      • IPA(key): /siˈɡaro/ [siˈɣ̞a.ro] (Latin America, Philippines)
      • Audio (Colombia):(file)
      • Rhymes: -aro
      • Syllabification: ci‧ga‧rro

      Noun

      [edit]

      cigarro m (plural cigarros)

      1. cigar (rolled bundle of tobacco made for smoking)
        Synonym: puro
      2. cigarette (thin roll of tobacco made for smoking)

      Derived terms

      [edit]
      • cigarrillo (diminutive)
      • cigarrito (diminutive)
      • cigarro de papel
